properties.name: Hobbiton
properties.lore: Holes and gardens on the slopes of the Hill, beside the Water.

properties.name: Bywater
properties.lore: A busy village where the Water meets the East Road; known for its inn.

properties.name: Overhill
properties.lore: A quiet hamlet on the far side of the Hill.

properties.name: Waymeet
properties.lore: A crossroads village in the Westfarthing where several lanes join the road.

properties.name: Michel Delving
properties.lore: The chief town of the Shire, dug into the White Downs.

properties.name: Little Delving
properties.lore: A smaller cousin of Michel Delving, further along the Downs.

properties.name: Needlehole
properties.lore: A village tucked among the woods of the north-west.

properties.name: Tuckborough
properties.lore: Old home of a great family, with many-tunnelled smials in the green hills.

properties.name: Longbottom
properties.lore: Warm southern fields where the best pipe-weed grows.

properties.name: Frogmorton
properties.lore: A road village of the Eastfarthing with a well-kept inn.

properties.name: Whitfurrows
properties.lore: Farmland and white furrows near the eastern end of the road.

properties.name: Scary
properties.lore: A village by old quarries in the Eastfarthing hills.

properties.name: Brockenborings
properties.lore: Hobbit-holes among rough northern hills.

properties.name: Stock
properties.lore: A marsh village at the edge of the Marish, close to the river.

properties.name: Woodhall
properties.lore: A village beneath the eaves of the Woody End.

properties.name: Bucklebury
properties.lore: The chief village of Buckland, across the river from the rest of the Shire.

properties.name: Brandywine Bridge
properties.lore: The great stone bridge that carries the East Road over the river.

properties.name: Bucklebury Ferry
properties.lore: A flat ferry that crosses the Brandywine below Stock.

properties.name: Withywindle
properties.lore: A dark, slow river winding through the heart of the Old Forest.

properties.name: Barrow-downs
properties.lore: Bare green hills crowned with ancient barrows and standing stones.

properties.name: Bree
properties.lore: The chief village of Bree-land, where the East Road meets the Greenway.

properties.name: Archet
properties.lore: The village on the edge of the Chetwood.

properties.name: Staddle
properties.lore: A village on the far slopes of Bree-hill, home to many hobbits.

properties.name: Combe
properties.lore: A village in a deep valley east of the hill.

properties.name: Chetwood
properties.lore: A wide wood north-east of Bree, rarely free of outlaws.

properties.name: Midgewater Marshes
properties.lore: Endless bog and biting insects east of Bree.

properties.name: Forsaken Inn
properties.lore: The last inn on the East Road, a day's ride beyond Bree.

properties.name: Tower Hills
properties.lore: Green hills crowned by old white towers that look towards the sea.
